2. The plaintiff filed written objection on 9-12-2003 against the application for return of the plaint. 

 3. The contention of the defendant is that the suit being a suit for mandatory injunction, damage and compensation for non-taking of delivery of cargo from the containers, it is not maintainable in this Admiralty Court, since the plaintiff is not a carrier of the goods nor the cause of action comes under the jurisdiction of this Court under any of the provision as provided in section 3 of the Admiralty Courts Act, 2000. 

 4. The learned Advocate Mr. Imtiaz Mahmood appearing on behalf of the defend-ant while takes this Court through the assertion made in the plaint further draws the attention of this Court to paragraph No.1 of the plaint and argues that except mentioning a sentence that the plaintiff carrier on business of shipping, nowhere in the four corners of the plaint the status of the plaintiff as carrier of the disputed consignment has been mentioned and therefore, this suit is not maintainable in this Admiralty Court. 

 5. The learned Advocate Mr Imtiaz Mahmood further argues that the cause of the suit, as alleged in the plaint, appears to have been arisen from the discharge of the cargo in the Chittagong Port which are kept in a container and the plaintiff raised allegations that the defendants have not taken delivery of the cargoes from the container and therefore, the plaint case is clearly indicative of that the cause of action arisen in respect of the containers which is neither a question relating to the carriage of goods by sea nor any use of the vessel and therefore, not amenable to the jurisdiction of this Court. 

 6. The learned Advocate Mr lmtiaz Mahmood contends that the jurisdiction of the Admiralty Court being a special statutory jurisdiction and the same have been detailed in section 3 of the Admiralty Courts Act, 2000, any cause to be brought before the Court must come within the provisions of the law. There-fore, even if the plaintiff has any cause of action against the defendant the plaintiff cannot bring a suit under the Admiralty jurisdiction and therefore, the plaint is liable to be returned. 

 7. Refuting the arguments made by the learned Advocated Mr Imtiaz Mahmood, the learned Advocate Mr Muhammad ()Mullah appearing on behalf of the plaintiff argues that only the mention of the status of the plaintiff is enough for the purpose of institution of the suit in the Admiralty Jurisdiction although the plaintiff not only mentioned in various paragraphs of the plaint about his status but also substantiated his status, by filing the documents specially the Bill of Lading where from it appears that the same has been issued by the plaintiff to the defendant. Therefore, the submission put forward that the plaintiff has not asserted the status within the four corner of the plaint has no basis. 

 8. The learned Advocate Mr Muhammad Ohiullah strenuously argues that the disputed cargo have been carried by the owner of the vessel, the plaintiff, and the same have been carried in the mother vessel 'MV. Unique' subsequently by the feeder vessel 'MV Banga Barat' and unless the plaintiff is a carrier, containers could not have been carried under the bills of lading issued by the plaintiff, therefore, the claim made by the plaintiff comes under the provision of 3(2)(Ja) of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 which is squarely tenable in the eye of law. 

 11. The plaintiff has brought this suit for mandatory injunction, for damage and compensation alleging inter alia that the defendant, being the consignee of the cargo of seed potato, came to a contract with the plaintiff for carriage of those cargo through the containers and the vessel owned by the plaintiff which the plaintiff did and the same when reached Chittagong Port the defendant denied to take delivery of the cargo on the plea of bar imposed by the plant protection wing of the Government of Bangladesh. Therefore, the plaintiff brought the suit before this Admiralty jurisdiction wherein the defendant also entered appearance and contesting the suit. It further appears from the material on records that upon an application filed by the plaintiff the cargo was destroyed during the pendency of the suit pursuant to the order passed by this Court. 

 12. It appears that the plaintiff brought the suit under the provision of section 3(2)(Ja) of 

 13. It appears that to maintain a suit in the Admiralty Court under the Provision of Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 the cause of action must attract the provision made in section 3 of the Admiralty Court, 2000, meaning thereby that the cause of action which can be prosecuted in the Admiralty Court must involve a claim amenable to the provision of section 3 of the said Act. The plaintiff herein since mentioned in the plaint that he is engaged in business of shipping and substantiated it by the document, filed by the plaintiff, showing that the disputed cargo has been carried by the plaintiff under the Bill of Lading issued in favour of the defendant, this Court notes that the dispute as has been brought before this Court has arisen from the contract of carriage of goods by sea and therefore amenable under the provision of section 3(2)(Ja) of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 and is clearly maintainable in this Admiralty Court. 

 14. The decision as made herein regarding the status of the plaintiff upon a prima facie consideration of the material on records, shall not bar the defendant to ask the point to be decided at the final stage of the suit, since the law provides that the question of maintainability since goes to the root of the case may be asked and considered upon obtaining evidence on dock.
